{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation produced the highest success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.562 s), with high Path Efficiency (0.502) and Average Speed (12.833 cm/s), and the highest Angular Dispersion (0.399).",
    "Bright Visual Only stimulation achieved the second-highest success rate (0.785), comparable to Combined, with slightly slower Time-to-Target (2.614 s) and moderate AD (0.387).",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only showed intermediate performance: success rates of 0.673 and 0.685, Time-to-Target around 3.0-3.1 s, and lower Path Efficiency (~0.43-0.44) than visual-combined conditions.",
    "Sham stimulation exhibited dramatically worse performance across all metrics: lowest success rate (0.273), slowest Time-to-Target (4.682 s), poorest Path Efficiency (0.308), slowest Average Speed (10.737 cm/s), and lowest Angular Dispersion (0.236).",
    "Angular Dispersion followed a clear hierarchy: Combined > Bright Visual Only > ICMS Only > Dim Visual Only > Sham, suggesting stimulation type modulates directional variability in movement.",
    "Sample sizes vary substantially across paradigms, with Combined dominating (n=48,846, 63.7% of data) versus Sham (n=3,505, 4.6% of data)."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) versus Combined (0.780) and Bright Visual Only (0.785) shows a 2.9-fold difference, the largest absolute gap across any variable.",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.682 s) is 1.83× slower than Combined (2.562 s), representing a 2.12 s absolute difference.",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) versus Combined (0.502) shows a 63% relative deficit, with Sham also 38% below Bright Visual Only (0.504).",
    "Angular Dispersion: Combined (0.399) is 69% higher than Sham (0.236), with Dim Visual Only (0.336) and ICMS Only (0.354) intermediate; this ordering inversely mirrors their Time-to-Target performance.",
    "Average Speed: Sham (10.737 cm/s) is 16% slower than Combined (12.833 cm/s), a smaller relative difference than other metrics, suggesting speed is less sensitive to stimulation condition than accuracy or efficiency."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Stimulation—whether combined multimodal or unimodal visual—substantially improves navigation performance over no stimulation. The Combined paradigm optimizes speed and success, while Bright Visual Only achieves nearly equivalent success with marginally slower responses. Intracortical microstimulation (ICMS) alone provides modest benefit over sham but underperforms relative to visual stimulation. Critically, higher Angular Dispersion in better-performing conditions suggests that effective navigation may tolerate or even require greater directional variability, possibly reflecting active exploration or correction behaviors absent in the slow, inefficient Sham trials. The pronounced Sham deficit indicates that the task is genuinely challenging without sensory augmentation, validating the stimulation's functional relevance.",
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes (Combined n=48,846 vs. Sham n=3,505) may affect precision of Sham estimates and complicate variance comparisons.",
    "No statistical tests (e.g., ANOVA, post-hoc comparisons) are provided; observed differences are descriptive only and significance is unverified.",
    "Missing information on mouse-level clustering—8 mice contributed unequally (range 7,233–10,986 rows)—so within-mouse correlation and individual differences are unaccounted for.",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme range (max 29.817) suggesting outliers or calculation anomalies that may distort means; no median or robust statistics are available.",
    "No information on trial sequence, learning effects, or session structure; performance may reflect training rather than pure stimulation effects.",
    "Temperature and prompt template factors (from run metadata) indicate this is LLM-generated data, potentially limiting generalizability to biological experiments."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept to account for clustering, followed by planned contrasts comparing each active stimulation to Sham and pairwise comparisons among active conditions. Report effect sizes (Cohen's d) and confidence intervals. Examine distributions of Path Efficiency for outliers and consider median-based robust statistics. If temporal data exist, analyze learning curves to disentangle stimulation effects from practice effects. Finally, model relationships between Angular Dispersion and other metrics (e.g., does higher AD predict better Success when controlling for Speed?) to test the exploratory hypothesis suggested by the descriptive pattern."
}
